correctness.rationale: The Pansiot adjacent-change code maps precisely the eight forbidden binary factors to Q={010,101,11111,01110}. The published finite-code avoidance criterion implies goodness; the prefix-free block code {0,1100,111100}, centered 6/7 zeros and its reversed copy avoid Q, and even transition parity yields two good palindromes for each distinct block word. T_h satisfies T_h=T_{h-1}+T_{h-4}+T_{h-6}; its unique dominant positive root factors via (x+1)(x^2-x+1)(x^3-x^2-1), giving T_h=Theta(psi^h). Palindromic first halves bound P_n<=G_ceil(n/2), and Baranwal et al. Theorem 19 gives G_n=Theta(psi^n). Two parity classes and finitely many low lengths handled explicitly. Independent small palindrome enumeration agrees through n=14; the infinite proof is the injection and published growth theorem.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Theorem 19 gives Theta(psi^n) for all good words, whose first-half bound yields only the upper bound. Periodic shift traces do not determine reversal-fixed finite words, and no inspected general reflection theorem supplies the lower bound.
